newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says more to EMU than deficit criteria.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says more to EMU than deficit criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that talk about the three percent deficit criterion for entry into European monetary union must not be seen in isolation.
Tietmeyer said one must look at the whole economic situtaiton of a country, including debt levels, to determine whether they are fit to join the new currency in 1999.
"Three is a very important indicator but it would be wrong to view it in isolation," Tietmeyer said of the three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) criterion in the Maastricht Treaty.
"Basically, it is a question of sustainability," Tietmeyer said of fulfilling fiscial criteria for the new currency.

Tietmeyer told a Bundesbank news conference after a fortnightly council meeting that the European Monetary Institute report due in the spring would take an overall view on the suitability of European nations to join EMU.
